Superseded actor-projection experiment. This page does not evaluate the corrected event representation. Open the corrected rerun.

MAST · combining score graphs

300 conversations · nine Jev score layers · 14 overlapping reference labels · two window sizes · no new scoring calls.

Finding: The current experiment does not establish a consistent advantage from combining all graph Laplacians. Averaging graph layers helps over score-only features on unseen frameworks, but a simple activity baseline performs similarly.
  • For both window sizes, score-only summaries outperform the average graph and joint Laplacian features on task-group cross-validation.
  • When a framework is held out, averaging graph layers outperforms scores-only, but has approximately the same macro AP as the activity-only baseline.
  • Requirement fulfillment has the highest observed held-framework-out macro AP among the nine individual layers at both window sizes. This ranking is exploratory, not selection on an untouched test set.
  • Joint use of all Laplacians does not consistently improve over averaging graph layers or using the strongest individual layer.
  • This particular projection, window summary and linear classifier has not demonstrated a consistent advantage attributable to combining Laplacians. These results do not rule out other graph representations.

129 of 4200 reference-label cells are masked because annotations disagree or are unknown. All 300 conversations remain; known labels are used independently.

AP is non-interpolated average precision, not accuracy. F1 uses a fixed 0.5 threshold on class-balanced logistic-regression outputs; probabilities are not calibrated.

All variants use identical splits and a fixed regularized logistic-regression classifier. Original conversations, model inputs, matrix sequences, fold models and held-out predictions are preserved. Window sizes are reported separately; no configuration was selected by test performance.
